Uniqueness of extremal almost periodic states on the injective type III1\mathrm{III}_{1} factor

Michael Hartglass∘ Address: ∘Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, Santa Clara University mhartglass@scu.edu and Brent Nelson∙ Address: ∙Department of Mathematics, Michigan State University brent@math.msu.edu
Abstract.

Let R∞R_{\infty} denote the Araki–Woods factor—the unique separable injective type III1\mathrm{III}_{1} factor. For extremal almost periodic states φ,ψ∈(R∞)∗\varphi,\psi\in(R_{\infty})_{*}, we show that if Δφ\Delta_{\varphi} and Δψ\Delta_{\psi} have the same point spectrum then ψ=φ∘α\psi=\varphi\circ\alpha for some α∈Aut​(R∞)\alpha\in\text{Aut}(R_{\infty}). Consequently, the extremal almost periodic states on R∞R_{\infty} are parameterized by countable dense subgroups of ℝ+\mathbb{R}_{+}, up to precomposition by automorphisms. As an application, we show that KMS states for generalized gauge actions on Cuntz algebras agree (up to an automorphism) with tensor products of Powers states on their von Neumann completions.

Introduction

Using approximations by completely positive maps, Haagerup provided a new proof in [Haa89] of the uniqueness of the separable injective type IIIλ\mathrm{III}_{\lambda} factors for 0<λ<10<\lambda<1. This uniqueness was first established by Connes in his celebrated work [Con76], but a novel consequence of Haagerup’s proof was the uniqueness of their 2​πlog⁡(1/λ)\frac{2\pi}{\log(1/\lambda)}-periodic states. For 0<λ≤10<\lambda\leq 1 denote

(1) (Rλ,φλ):=⨂n∈ℕ(M2​(ℂ),ϕλ)\displaystyle(R_{\lambda},\varphi_{\lambda}):=\bigotimes_{n\in\mathbb{N}}(M_{2}(\mathbb{C}),\phi_{\lambda})

where

ϕλ​(x):=Tr​[(11+λ00λ1+λ)​x].\phi_{\lambda}(x):=\text{Tr}\left[\left(\begin{array}[]{cc}\frac{1}{1+\lambda}&0\\ 0&\frac{\lambda}{1+\lambda}\end{array}\right)x\right].

These are separable injective factors of type IIIλ\mathrm{III}_{\lambda} for 0<λ<10<\lambda<1 (also known as Powers’ factors having been first studied in [Pow67]), and type II1\mathrm{II}_{1} for λ=1\lambda=1. The associated states are 2​πlog⁡(1/λ)\frac{2\pi}{\log(1/\lambda)}-periodic for 0<λ<10<\lambda<1, while τ:=φ1\tau:=\varphi_{1} is of course the unique tracial state on R:=R1R:=R_{1}. For (N,φ)(N,\varphi) a separable injective type IIIλ\mathrm{III}_{\lambda} factor equipped with a 2​πlog⁡(1/λ)\frac{2\pi}{\log(1/\lambda)}-periodic state and 0<λ<10<\lambda<1, Haagerup established a state-preserving isomorphism (N,φ)≅(Rλ,φλ)(N,\varphi)\cong(R_{\lambda},\varphi_{\lambda}), and consequently any pair of 2​πlog⁡(1/λ)\frac{2\pi}{\log(1/\lambda)}-periodic states on RλR_{\lambda} differ only by precomposition with an automorphism (see [Haa89, Theorem 6.1 and Corollary 6.5]). Haagerup also established the uniqueness of the separable injective type III1\mathrm{III}_{1} factor in [Haa87] using a reduction due to Connes in [Con85], and a second proof was published posthumously in [Haa16] that more closely followed the approach in [Haa89]. However, neither of these proofs provide a state preserving isomorphism and consequently the analogue of [Haa89, Corollary 6.5] has been missing in the type III1\mathrm{III}_{1} setting until now. In this article we prove such an analogue, where periodic states are replaced with so-called extremal almost periodic states.

In [Con74], Connes defined an almost periodic weight as a faithful normal semifinite weight φ\varphi whose modular operator Δφ\Delta_{\varphi} is diagonalizable:

Δφ=∑λ∈Sd​(φ)λ​1{λ}​(Δφ),\Delta_{\varphi}=\sum_{\lambda\in\text{Sd}(\varphi)}\lambda 1_{\{\lambda\}}(\Delta_{\varphi}),

where we denote the point spectrum of Δφ\Delta_{\varphi} by Sd​(φ)\text{Sd}(\varphi). An extremal weight is one whose centralizer subalgebra Mφ:={x∈M:σtφ​(x)=x​∀t∈ℝ}M^{\varphi}:=\{x\in M\colon\sigma_{t}^{\varphi}(x)=x\ \forall t\in\mathbb{R}\} is a factor. Almost periodic weights have the property that (Mφ)′∩M=(Mφ)′∩Mφ(M^{\varphi})^{\prime}\cap M=(M^{\varphi})^{\prime}\cap M^{\varphi} (see [Con72, Theorem 10]), and so extremal almost periodic weights only occur on factors. Additionally, Sd​(φ)\text{Sd}(\varphi) for an extremal almost periodic weight φ\varphi is a subgroup of ℝ+\mathbb{R}_{+}, the group of positive reals (0,∞)(0,\infty) under multiplication (see, for example, [Dyk97, Lemma 4.9]). The states φλ\varphi_{\lambda} in (1) are extremal almost periodic: for λ<1\lambda<1 this follows from [Con73, Theorem 4.2.6]; and τ\tau is tracial so that Δτ=1\Delta_{\tau}=1 and Rτ=RR^{\tau}=R. Aperiodic examples of extremal almost periodic weights necessarily occur on type III1\mathrm{III}_{1} factors, and, while not all type III1\mathrm{III}_{1} factors admit such weights (see [Con74, Corollary 5.3]), the unique separable injective type III1\mathrm{III}_{1} factor R∞R_{\infty} (also known as the Araki–Woods factor) has many. To see this, extend the notation in (1) to λ>1\lambda>1 by letting ϕλ:=ϕ1/λ\phi_{\lambda}:=\phi_{1/\lambda} and (Rλ,φλ):=(R1/λ,φ1/λ)(R_{\lambda},\varphi_{\lambda}):=(R_{1/\lambda},\varphi_{1/\lambda}). For a countable subgroup Λ≤ℝ+\Lambda\leq\mathbb{R}_{+}, denote

(2) (RΛ,φΛ):=⨂λ∈Λ(Rλ,φλ).\displaystyle(R_{\Lambda},\varphi_{\Lambda}):=\bigotimes_{\lambda\in\Lambda}(R_{\lambda},\varphi_{\lambda}).

If Λ\Lambda is of the form λℤ\lambda^{\mathbb{Z}} for some 0<λ≤10<\lambda\leq 1, then (RΛ,φΛ)≅(Rλ,φλ)(R_{\Lambda},\varphi_{\Lambda})\cong(R_{\lambda},\varphi_{\lambda}) thanks to the property (Rλ​⊗¯​Rλ,φλ⊗φλ)=(Rλ,φλ)(R_{\lambda}\bar{\otimes}R_{\lambda},\varphi_{\lambda}\otimes\varphi_{\lambda})=(R_{\lambda},\varphi_{\lambda}). Otherwise, Λ\Lambda is dense in ℝ+\mathbb{R}_{+} and RΛ≅R∞R_{\Lambda}\cong R_{\infty}. Moreover, φΛ\varphi_{\Lambda} is an extremal almost periodic state (see, for example, [HI22, Lemma 5.2.(i)]). Our main result is the following:

Theorem A.

Let NN be a diffuse separable injective factor equipped with an extremal almost periodic state φ\varphi. Then

(N,φ)≅(RΛ,φΛ)(N,\varphi)\cong(R_{\Lambda},\varphi_{\Lambda})

where Λ=Sd​(φ)\Lambda=\text{Sd}(\varphi).

If Λ=λℤ\Lambda=\lambda^{\mathbb{Z}} for some 0<λ≤10<\lambda\leq 1 then the above is simply either [Haa89, Theorem 6.1] for λ<1\lambda<1 or [Con76, Theorem 1] for λ=1\lambda=1. Thus the novelty of the above theorem lies only in the case that Λ\Lambda is dense in ℝ+\mathbb{R}_{+}, but nevertheless our proof simultaneously covers all cases. The proof of Theorem A very closely follows Haagerup’s proof of [Haa89, Theorem 6.1] and can be found in Section 5. Roughly, the strategy is to approximate a countable generating set for NN by a sequence of finite dimensional subfactors that when equipped with the restriction of φ\varphi are isomorphic to a finite dimensional tensor factor of (RΛ,φΛ)(R_{\Lambda},\varphi_{\Lambda}). These subfactors are constructed using approximate completely positive factorizations of the identity map through matrix algebras, whose existence is established in Section 3 (paralleling [Haa89, Section 5]). Notably, Lemma 3.1 marks a technical deviation from Haagerup’s ideas, though it still essentially corresponds to [Haa89, Lemma 5.3]. These completely positive maps also respect the modular theory of φ\varphi, a property which is needed to apply the results in Section 4 (paralleling [Haa89, Section 4]). These results, namely Theorem 4.4, approximate the completely positive maps by x↦∑n=1∞an∗​x​anx\mapsto\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_{n}^{*}xa_{n} for (an)n∈ℕ⊂Nφ(a_{n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subset N^{\varphi} a partition of unity, which in turn allows one to further approximate the maps by an inner automorphism using the notion of δ\delta-related tuples from [Haa89, Section 2]. Despite how similar our results are to those in [Haa89], working with non-cyclic subgroups of ℝ+\mathbb{R}_{+} almost always prevents us from simply citing the corresponding results. So instead the details are presented in full and the reader should find the paper mostly self-contained.

We also remark that if one could directly argue that a separable injective type III1\mathrm{III}_{1} factor admits at least one extremal almost periodic state, then Theorem A would yield a new proof of the uniqueness of such factors. However, this remains out of reach. In fact, Haagerup’s approach in [Haa87] specifically avoids this by working instead with dominant weights, which are known to always exist for properly infinite factors by [CT77, Chapter II].

As an immediate consequence of Theorem A we have the following.

Corollary B.

If φ\varphi and ψ\psi are extremal almost periodic states on R∞R_{\infty} with Sd​(φ)=Sd​(ψ)\text{Sd}(\varphi)=\text{Sd}(\psi), then there exists α∈Aut​(R∞)\alpha\in\text{Aut}(R_{\infty}) satisfying ψ=φ∘α\psi=\varphi\circ\alpha.

This corollary combined with the existence of the extremal almost periodic states φΛ\varphi_{\Lambda} in (2) implies there is a one-to-one correspondence between the collection of countable dense subgroups of ℝ+\mathbb{R}_{+} and the equivalence classes of extremal almost periodic states on R∞R_{\infty} under precomposition by automorphisms.

Due to its uniqueness, R∞R_{\infty} arises from a variety of constructions, and so our results can be used to recognize extremal almost periodic states on these constructions as some φΛ\varphi_{\Lambda}. Our last main result is an example of this involving the Cuntz algebra. If JJ is any finite or countably infinite set, then recall that the Cuntz algebra, 𝒪J\mathcal{O}_{J}, is the universal C*-algebra generated by a family of isometries {vj}j∈J\{v_{j}\}_{j\in J} with mutually orthogonal ranges, and if JJ is finite it is further required that ∑j∈Jvj​vj∗=1\sum_{j\in J}v_{j}v_{j}^{*}=1. Let μ:J→(0,1)\mu\colon J\to(0,1) be a function with the property that ∑j∈Jμ⁡(j)=1\sum_{j\in J}\mu(j)=1. Define a gauge action ℝ​↷𝜎​𝒪J\mathbb{R}\overset{\sigma}{\curvearrowright}\mathcal{O}_{J} by

σt​(vj)=μ​(j)i​t​vj,\sigma_{t}(v_{j})=\mu(j)^{it}v_{j},

for each t∈ℝt\in\mathbb{R} and j∈Jj\in J. It is known that a unique KMS state φ\varphi exists for such an action (see, for example, [Tho17]). Letting πφ\pi_{\varphi} be its GNS representation, we will abuse notation slightly and let φ\varphi also denote its extension to πφ​(𝒪J)′′\pi_{\varphi}(\mathcal{O}_{J})^{\prime\prime} as a faithful normal state. Denote by Λ\Lambda the multiplicative subgroup of ℝ+\mathbb{R}_{+} generated by μ⁡(J)\mu(J). It has been shown by Izumi for JJ finite [Izu93] and Thomsen for JJ infinite [Tho19] that πφ​(𝒪J)′′\pi_{\varphi}(\mathcal{O}_{J})^{\prime\prime} is a separable injective factor of type IIIλ\mathrm{III}_{\lambda} if Λ=λℤ\Lambda=\lambda^{\mathbb{Z}} for some λ∈(0,1)\lambda\in(0,1) and of type III1\mathrm{III}_{1} otherwise. In the former case, [Haa89, Theorem 6.1] implies (πφ​(𝒪J)′′,φ)≅(Rλ,φλ)(\pi_{\varphi}(\mathcal{O}_{J})^{\prime\prime},\varphi)\cong(R_{\lambda},\varphi_{\lambda}) since φ\varphi is necessarily 2​πlog⁡(1/λ)\frac{2\pi}{\log(1/\lambda)}-periodic. In the general case we argue in Section 6 that Theorem A can be applied to obtain the following.

Theorem C.

With the above notation, φ\varphi is an extremal almost periodic state on πφ​(𝒪J)′′\pi_{\varphi}(\mathcal{O}_{J})^{\prime\prime} and there is a state preserving isomorphism (πφ​(𝒪J)′′,φ)≅(RΛ,φΛ)(\pi_{\varphi}(\mathcal{O}_{J})^{\prime\prime},\varphi)\cong(R_{\Lambda},\varphi_{\Lambda}).

1. Preliminaries

We say a von Neumann algebra MM is separable if it is separable in the weak* topology induced by M≅(M∗)∗M\cong(M_{*})^{*}; equivalently, if M∗M_{*} is separable as a Banach space. We write N≤MN\leq M when NN is a unital von Neumann subalgebra of MM. For a family of subalgebras {Ni≤M:i∈I}\{N_{i}\leq M\colon i\in I\}, we write ⋁i∈INi\bigvee_{i\in I}N_{i} for the von Neumann algebra generated by ⋃i∈INi\bigcup_{i\in I}N_{i}. For a state φ\varphi on MM we define the inner product

⟨x,y⟩φ=φ⁡(y∗​x)x,y∈M,\left\langle x,y\right\rangle_{\varphi}=\varphi(y^{*}x)\qquad x,y\in M,

and denote its associated norm by ‖x‖φ\|x\|_{\varphi}.

We assume the reader has some familiarity with weights and modular theory, but the complete details can be found in [Tak03] (see also [GLN24, Section 1]). For a faithful normal semifinite weight on MM, its modular automorphism group refers to the action ℝ​↷σφ​M\mathbb{R}\overset{\sigma^{\varphi}}{\curvearrowright}M defined by

σtφ​(x):=Δφi​t​x​Δφ−i​t.\sigma_{t}^{\varphi}(x):=\Delta_{\varphi}^{it}x\Delta_{\varphi}^{-it}.

We say a subalgebra N≤MN\leq M is φ\varphi-invariant if φ|N\varphi|_{N} is semifinite and σtφ​(N)=N\sigma_{t}^{\varphi}(N)=N for all t∈ℝt\in\mathbb{R}, which is equivalent to the existence of a faithful normal φ\varphi-invariant conditional expectation from MM onto NN (see [Tak03, Theorem IX.4.2]). For λ∈ℝ+\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_{+} we denote

M(φ,λ):={x∈M:σtφ​(x)=λi​t​x​∀t∈ℝ},M^{(\varphi,\lambda)}:=\{x\in M\colon\sigma_{t}^{\varphi}(x)=\lambda^{it}x\ \forall t\in\mathbb{R}\},

so that M(φ,1)=MφM^{(\varphi,1)}=M^{\varphi}. We call such elements eigenoperators of φ\varphi. We also denote

M(φ,eig):=span​(⋃λ∈ℝ+M(φ,λ)),M^{(\varphi,\text{eig})}:=\text{span}\left(\bigcup_{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_{+}}M^{(\varphi,\lambda)}\right),

which is a unital ∗*-subalgebra of MM, and it is weak* dense when φ\varphi is almost periodic (see [GLN24, Lemma 1.4]).

Given an almost periodic weight φ\varphi on MM, let Λ≤ℝ+\Lambda\leq\mathbb{R}_{+} be the group generated by Sd​(φ)\text{Sd}(\varphi). Equipping Λ\Lambda with the discrete topology, let GG denote its compact dual group. Identifying the dual of ℝ+\mathbb{R}_{+} with ℝ\mathbb{R} via the pairing (s,t)=si​t(s,t)=s^{it}, the transpose of the inclusion map ι:Λ→ℝ+\iota\colon\Lambda\to\mathbb{R}_{+} gives a continuous group homomorphsim ι^:ℝ→G\hat{\iota}\colon\mathbb{R}\to G determined by

(ι^​(t)|λ)=(ι⁡(λ)|t)=λi​t.(\hat{\iota}(t)|\lambda)=(\iota(\lambda)|t)=\lambda^{it}.

The action ℝ​↷σφ​M\mathbb{R}\overset{\sigma^{\varphi}}{\curvearrowright}M given by the modular automorphism group of φ\varphi determines an action G​↷𝛼​MG\overset{\alpha}{\curvearrowright}M satisfying αι^​(t)=σtφ\alpha_{\hat{\iota}(t)}=\sigma_{t}^{\varphi} for all t∈ℝt\in\mathbb{R}. In particular, Mα=MφM^{\alpha}=M^{\varphi} and more generally for x∈M(φ,λ)x\in M^{(\varphi,\lambda)} one has αs​(x)=(λ|s)​x\alpha_{s}(x)=(\lambda|s)x for all s∈Gs\in G. We call this action of GG the point modular extension of ℝ​↷σφ​M\mathbb{R}\overset{\sigma^{\varphi}}{\curvearrowright}M. For each λ∈Λ\lambda\in\Lambda, there is a normal MφM^{\varphi}-MφM^{\varphi}-bimodular idempotent map ℰ(φ,λ):M→M(φ,λ)\mathcal{E}_{(\varphi,\lambda)}\colon M\to M^{(\varphi,\lambda)} defined by

ℰ(φ,λ)​(x):=∫G(λ|s)¯​αs​(x)​𝑑μ​(s),\mathcal{E}_{(\varphi,\lambda)}(x):=\int_{G}\overline{(\lambda|s)}\alpha_{s}(x)\ d\mu(s),

where μ\mu is a normalized Haar measure on GG. In particular, ℰφ:=ℰ(φ,1)\mathcal{E}_{\varphi}:=\mathcal{E}_{(\varphi,1)} is the unique φ\varphi-preserving faithful normal conditional expectation onto the centralizer. If φ\varphi is a state, then one also has

‖x‖φ2=∑λ∈Λ‖ℰ(φ,λ)​(x)‖φ2,\|x\|_{\varphi}^{2}=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\|\mathcal{E}_{(\varphi,\lambda)}(x)\|_{\varphi}^{2},

for all x∈Mx\in M since Δφ=∑λ∈Λ1{λ}​(Δφ)\Delta_{\varphi}=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1_{\{\lambda\}}(\Delta_{\varphi}). See [Dyk95, Dyk97] for additional details.

Suppose that FF is a finite-dimensional subfactor of a factor NN, and FcF^{c} is defined by Fc=F′∩NF^{c}=F^{\prime}\cap N. Note that this means N≅F⊗FcN\cong F\otimes F^{c}. For a faithful normal state φ\varphi on NN, the following three conditions are equivalent (see, for example, [Haa89, Section 4]):

  1. (1)

    FF is Δφ\Delta_{\varphi}-invariant;

  2. (2)

    there exists a φ\varphi-preserving conditional expectation from NN onto FF;

  3. (3)

    (N,φ)≅(F,φ)⊗(Fc,φ)(N,\varphi)\cong(F,\varphi)\otimes(F^{c},\varphi).

For the purposes of this article, condition (3) above will be the one which is easiest to exploit. We will denote this more compactly as φ=φ|F⊗φ|Fc\varphi=\varphi|_{F}\otimes\varphi|_{F^{c}}.

2. Extremal almost periodic weights

In this section we present a few ways to construct new extremal almost periodic weights out of old ones. We will only need to apply them to states in the present article, but we prove them in the generality of weights whenever possible because they may be of independent interest. The following lemma is proven in [HI22, Lemma 5.2.(ii)] in the case of states and for M=R∞M=R_{\infty} the Araki–Woods factor. However, the proof in the generality below is exactly the same.

Lemma 2.1.

Let (M,φ)(M,\varphi) be a von Neumann algebra equipped with an extremal almost periodic weight. If (N,ψ)(N,\psi) is a factor equipped with an almost periodic weight satisfying Sd​(ψ)⊂Sd​(φ)\text{Sd}(\psi)\subset\text{Sd}(\varphi), then φ⊗ψ\varphi\otimes\psi is extremal almost periodic on M​⊗¯​NM\bar{\otimes}N with Sd​(φ⊗ψ)=Sd​(φ)\text{Sd}(\varphi\otimes\psi)=\text{Sd}(\varphi).

The following can be viewed as a partial converse to the previous lemma.

Lemma 2.2.

Let M=P​⊗¯​NM=P\bar{\otimes}N be factor with PP a type I\mathrm{I} factor. Suppose φ\varphi is an extremal almost periodic weight on MM satisfying: φ|P\varphi|_{P} and φ|N\varphi|_{N} are seminifinite; φ|P\varphi|_{P} is almost periodic; and φ=φ|P⊗φ|N\varphi=\varphi|_{P}\otimes\varphi|_{N}. Then φ|N\varphi|_{N} is extremal almost periodic with Sd​(φ|N)=Sd​(φ)\text{Sd}(\varphi|_{N})=\text{Sd}(\varphi). In particular, Sd​(φ|P)⊂Sd​(φ|N)\text{Sd}(\varphi|_{P})\subset\text{Sd}(\varphi|_{N}).

Proof.

Identifying P≅B⁡(ℋ)P\cong B(\mathcal{H}) for some Hilbert space ℋ\mathcal{H}, we have that φ|P​(x)=Tr​(h12​x​h12)\varphi|_{P}(x)=\text{Tr}(h^{\frac{1}{2}}xh^{\frac{1}{2}}) for some positive (unbounded) operator hh on ℋ\mathcal{H} and σtφ|P​(x)=hi​t​x​h−i​t\sigma_{t}^{\varphi|_{P}}(x)=h^{it}xh^{-it} for all t∈ℝt\in\mathbb{R}. Since φ|P\varphi|_{P} is almost periodic, hh is necessarily diagonalizable with respect to some family of matrix units {ei,j∈B(ℋ):i,j∈I}\{e_{i,j}\in B(\mathcal{H})\colon i,j\in I\}, In particular one has ei,i⊗1∈Mφe_{i,i}\otimes 1\in M^{\varphi} for all i∈Ii\in I. Because (N,φ|N)(N,\varphi|_{N}) can be identified with ((ei,i⊗1)​M​(ei,i⊗1),1Tr​(h​ei,i)​φ)((e_{i,i}\otimes 1)M(e_{i,i}\otimes 1),\frac{1}{\text{Tr}(he_{i,i})}\varphi) for any i∈Ii\in I, it follows from [GLN24, Remark 1.5] that φ|N\varphi|_{N} is extremal almost periodic.

Next, we see that ei,je_{i,j} is an eigenoperator of φ|P\varphi|_{P} for each i,j∈Ii,j\in I since hh is diagonalized with respect to these matrix units, say with eigenvalue λi,j\lambda_{i,j}. Note that λj,i=1/λi,j\lambda_{j,i}=1/\lambda_{i,j}. Using that MφM^{\varphi} is a factor we have ei,i​Mφ​ej,j=ei,j⊗Ne_{i,i}M^{\varphi}e_{j,j}=e_{i,j}\otimes N is non-zero for each i,j∈Ii,j\in I. Hence there is a non-zero x∈Nx\in N with ei,j⊗x∈Mφe_{i,j}\otimes x\in M^{\varphi}, and the factorization φ=φ|P⊗φ|N\varphi=\varphi|_{P}\otimes\varphi|_{N} implies x∈N(φ|N,1/λi,j)=N(φ|N,λj,i)x\in N^{(\varphi|_{N},1/\lambda_{i,j})}=N^{(\varphi|_{N},\lambda_{j,i})}. Consequently,

Sd(φ|P)={λi,j:i,j∈I}⊂Sd(φ|N).\text{Sd}(\varphi|_{P})=\{\lambda_{i,j}\colon i,j\in I\}\subset\text{Sd}(\varphi|_{N}).

Since Sd​(φ|N)\text{Sd}(\varphi|_{N}) is a group and Sd​(φ)=Sd​(φ|P)​Sd​(φ|N)\text{Sd}(\varphi)=\text{Sd}(\varphi|_{P})\text{Sd}(\varphi|_{N}), it follows that Sd​(φ|N)=Sd​(φ)\text{Sd}(\varphi|_{N})=\text{Sd}(\varphi) as claimed. ∎

Observe that if φ\varphi in previous lemma is a state, then of course its restrictions to PP and NN are automatically semifinite, but also φ|P=Tr​(h12⋅h12)\varphi|_{P}=\text{Tr}(h^{\frac{1}{2}}\,\cdot\,h^{\frac{1}{2}}) is automatically almost periodic since hh is necessarily trace class and hence diagonalizable.

Lemma 2.3.

Let MM be a factor with separable predual equipped with an extremal almost periodic weight φ\varphi, let {pi∈Mφ:i∈I}\{p_{i}\in M^{\varphi}\colon i\in I\} be a family of projections satisfying ∑ipi=1\sum_{i}p_{i}=1, and let {μi∈ℝ+:i∈I}\{\mu_{i}\in\mathbb{R}_{+}\colon i\in I\} satisfy μiμj∈Sd​(φ)\frac{\mu_{i}}{\mu_{j}}\in\text{Sd}(\varphi) for all i,j∈Ii,j\in I. Set

h:=∑i∈Iμi​pi.h:=\sum_{i\in I}\mu_{i}p_{i}.

Then ψ:=φ⁡(h12⋅h12)\psi:=\varphi(h^{\frac{1}{2}}\,\cdot\,h^{\frac{1}{2}}) is an extremal almost periodic weight with Sd​(ψ)=Sd​(φ)\text{Sd}(\psi)=\text{Sd}(\varphi).

Proof.

The weight ψ\psi is faithful since hh is non-singular, and since φ\varphi is strictly semifinite and pi​Mφ​pi⊂Mψp_{i}M^{\varphi}p_{i}\subset M^{\psi} it follows that ψ\psi is also strictly semifinite. Observe that M(ψ,eig)M^{(\psi,\text{eig})} contains span{piM(φ,eig)pj:i,j∈I}\text{span}\{p_{i}M^{(\varphi,\text{eig})}p_{j}\colon i,j\in I\} and is therefore weak* dense. Consequently, ψ\psi is almost periodic by [GLN24, Lemma 1.4].

We next compute Sd​(ψ)\text{Sd}(\psi). Denote Λ:=Sd​(φ)\Lambda:=\text{Sd}(\varphi), which is a group by virtue of φ\varphi being extremal. Fix λ∈Λ\lambda\in\Lambda and i∈Ii\in I and note that there exists a partial isometry v∈M(φ,λ)v\in M^{(\varphi,\lambda)}. Since v∗​vv^{*}v and pip_{i} are not centrally orthogonal in MφM^{\varphi}, we can find a non-zero partial isometry w∈Mφw\in M^{\varphi} satisfying w∗​w≤piw^{*}w\leq p_{i} and w​w∗≤v∗​vww^{*}\leq v^{*}v. Hence v∗​v​w​pi=wv^{*}vwp_{i}=w, and in particular v​w​pivwp_{i} is a non-zero partial isometry. Since v​w​pi​w∗​v∗vwp_{i}w^{*}v^{*} and pip_{i} are also not centrally orthogonal in MφM^{\varphi}, we can find another partial isometry u∈Mφu\in M^{\varphi} satisfying u∗​u≤v​w​pi​w∗​v∗u^{*}u\leq vwp_{i}w^{*}v^{*} and u​u∗≤piuu^{*}\leq p_{i}. Hence pi​u​v​w​pi​w∗​v∗=up_{i}uvwp_{i}w^{*}v^{*}=u, and in particular pi​u​v​w​pi≠0p_{i}uvwp_{i}\neq 0. Also, the Connes cocycle derivative theorem implies

σtψ​(pi​u​v​w​pi)=hi​t​σtφ​(pi​u​v​w​pi)​h−i​t=μii​t​pi​u​σtφ​(v)​w​pi​μi−i​t=λi​t​pi​u​v​w​pi.\sigma_{t}^{\psi}(p_{i}uvwp_{i})=h^{it}\sigma_{t}^{\varphi}(p_{i}uvwp_{i})h^{-it}=\mu_{i}^{it}p_{i}u\sigma_{t}^{\varphi}(v)wp_{i}\mu_{i}^{-it}=\lambda^{it}p_{i}uvwp_{i}.

Hence Λ⊂Sd​(ψ)\Lambda\subset\text{Sd}(\psi). 3. Modular completely positive factorizations through matrix algebras

Given a (N,φ)(N,\varphi), a diffuse separable injective factor equipped with an extremal almost periodic state, we show in this section that the identity map on NN can be pointwise approximated in ∥⋅∥φ\|\cdot\|_{\varphi}-norm by a composition of completely maps to and from matrix algebras, which also respect the modular theory of φ\varphi. This result, Thoerem 3.2, corresponds to [Haa89, Theorem 5.1] and will be needed in the proof of Theorem A.

As an initial step, we first show such an approximations exist for completely positive maps to and from the unique separable injective type II1\mathrm{II}_{1} factor RR. The following lemma, which corresponds to [Haa89, Lemma 5.3], is where the hypothesis of almost periodicity is most heavily used in the form of the point modular extension of the modular automorphism group of φ\varphi and the existence of the idempotent maps ℰ(φ,λ)\mathcal{E}_{(\varphi,\lambda)} for λ∈Sd​(φ)\lambda\in\text{Sd}(\varphi).

4. Approximate Kraus representations

For (N,φ)(N,\varphi) a diffuse factor equipped with an extremal almost periodic state, the results in this section concern φ\varphi-invariant finite dimensional subfactors F≤NF\leq N and normal unital completely positive maps T:F→NT\colon F\to N that are compatible with φ\varphi and its modular theory. We note that Theorem 3.2 yields such maps after using Lemma 2.5 to identify 𝕄E⊗\mathbb{M}_{E}^{\otimes} with such a subfactor F≤NF\leq N.

Our first lemma, corresponds to [Haa89, Lemma 4.4], which shows such maps TT admit Kraus representations that use only elements of the centralizer NφN^{\varphi}.

for bi,j∈Nb_{i,j}\in N and

The next pair of lemmas are relative Dixmier norm approximation results. These relate to [Haa89, Corollary 3.4 and Lemma 4.5], respectively, but are necessarily weaker in the case that Sd​(φ)\text{Sd}(\varphi) is dense in ℝ+\mathbb{R}_{+} (see the proof of [Haa89, Theorem 3.1]).

Lemma 4.2.

Let NN be a diffuse factor with an extremal almost periodic state φ\varphi. For any finite set x1,…,xn∈N(φ,eig)x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}\in N^{(\varphi,\text{eig})} and ϵ>0\epsilon>0 there exists α∈conv⁡{Ad​(u):u∈Nφ}\alpha\in\conv\{\text{Ad}\left(u\right)\colon u\in N^{\varphi}\} satisfying

for each k=1,…,nk=1,\ldots,n.

Proof.

We first observe that for λ∈ℝ+\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_{+} and x∈N(φ,λ)x\in N^{(\varphi,\lambda)} one has

φ(x)∈conv{u∗xu|u∈U(NOPENφ)}¯∥⋅∥.\varphi(x)\in\overline{\conv\{u^{*}xu\,|\,u\in U(N_{\varphi)}\}}^{\|\cdot\|}.

Indeed, for λ=1\lambda=1 this is simply the Dixmier approximation theorem for type II1\mathrm{II}_{1} factors (see [Dix81, Section III.5.1]), and for λ≠1\lambda\neq 1 this follows from the same argument as in the proof of [Haa89, Lemma 3.2]. (Note that NφN^{\varphi} is indeed a type II1\mathrm{II}_{1} factor by [GLN24, Lemma 3.1].)

Now, let E⊂Sd​(φ)E\subset\text{Sd}(\varphi) be the necessarily finite set such that x1,…,xn∈span​{N(φ,λ):λ∈E}x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}\in\text{span}\{N^{(\varphi,\lambda)}\colon\lambda\in E\}, and for each k=1,…,nk=1,\ldots,n write xk=∑λ∈Exk,λx_{k}=\sum_{\lambda\in E}x_{k,\lambda} where xk,λ∈N(φ,λ)∪{0}x_{k,\lambda}\in N^{(\varphi,\lambda)}\cup\{0\}. Iteratively applying our initial observation through some enumeration of {1,…,n}×E\{1,\ldots,n\}\times E yields α∈conv⁡{Ad​(u):u∈Nφ}\alpha\in\conv\{\text{Ad}\left(u\right)\colon u\in N^{\varphi}\} satisfying

‖α⁡(xk,λ)−φ⁡(xk,λ)‖<ϵ|E|\|\alpha(x_{k,\lambda})-\varphi(x_{k,\lambda})\|<\frac{\epsilon}{|E|}

for each k=1,…,nk=1,\ldots,n and λ∈E\lambda\in E, and so the claimed inequality for xkx_{k} follows. ∎

Lemma 4.3.

Let NN be a diffuse factor equipped with an extremal almost periodic state φ\varphi, and let F≤NF\leq N be a finite dimensional subfactor for which

φ=φ|F⊗φ|Fc.\varphi=\varphi|_{F}\otimes\varphi|_{F^{c}}.

If ℰF:N→F\mathcal{E}_{F}\colon N\to F is the φ\varphi-invariant conditional expectation, then for all x∈N(φ,eig)x\in N^{(\varphi,\text{eig})} and ϵ>0\epsilon>0 there exists α∈conv⁡{Ad​(u):u∈𝒰⁡(Fc∩Nφ)}\alpha\in\conv\{\text{Ad}\left(u\right)\colon u\in\mathcal{U}(F^{c}\cap N^{\varphi})\} satisfying

‖α⁡(x)−ℰF​(x)‖<ϵ.\|\alpha(x)-\mathcal{E}_{F}(x)\|<\epsilon.
Proof.

For x∈N(φ,eig)x\in N^{(\varphi,\text{eig})} write

x=∑λ∈Exλ,x=\sum_{\lambda\in E}x_{\lambda},

where xλ∈N(φ,λ)x_{\lambda}\in N^{(\varphi,\lambda)} for each λ\lambda in a finite subset E⊂Sd​(φ)E\subset\text{Sd}(\varphi). Fix a family of matrix units {ei,j:1≤i,j≤d}\{e_{i,j}\colon 1\leq i,j\leq d\} for FF consisting of eigenoperators for σφ|F\sigma^{\varphi|_{F}}. In fact, φ=φ|F⊗φ|Fc\varphi=\varphi|_{F}\otimes\varphi|_{F^{c}} implies they will also be eigenoperators for σφ\sigma^{\varphi}, say σtφ​(ei,j)=λi,ji​t​ei,j\sigma_{t}^{\varphi}(e_{i,j})=\lambda_{i,j}^{it}e_{i,j} for λi,j∈Sd​(φ)\lambda_{i,j}\in\text{Sd}(\varphi). For each λ∈E\lambda\in E write

xλ=∑i,j=1dei,j​xi,j(λ),x_{\lambda}=\sum_{i,j=1}^{d}e_{i,j}x_{i,j}^{(\lambda)},

where xi,j(λ)∈Fcx_{i,j}^{(\lambda)}\in F^{c} for all 1≤i,j≤d1\leq i,j\leq d. Our choice of matrix units and xλ∈N(φ,λ)x_{\lambda}\in N^{(\varphi,\lambda)} implies xi,j(λ)∈N(φ,λλi,j)x_{i,j}^{(\lambda)}\in N^{(\varphi,\frac{\lambda}{\lambda_{i,j}})} for each 1≤i,j≤d1\leq i,j\leq d. Also, the tensor decomposition of φ\varphi implies

The following theorem is our main result in this section and corresponds to [Haa89, Theorem 4.1]. Recall that Lemma 4.1 gave an exact Kraus representation of the completely positive map T⁡(x)=∑j=1naj∗​x​ajT(x)=\sum_{j=1}^{n}a_{j}^{*}xa_{j} for a1,…,an∈Nφa_{1},\ldots,a_{n}\in N^{\varphi}. Since TT is unital, we in particular have that ∑j=1naj∗​aj=1\sum_{j=1}^{n}a_{j}^{*}a_{j}=1. However, ∑j=1naj​aj∗=1\sum_{j=1}^{n}a_{j}a_{j}^{*}=1 may fail to hold, and it will be needed in the proof of Theorem A to apply [Haa89, Theorem 2.3]. In the following theorem, we obtain this latter relation by sacrificing our exact finite Kraus representation for an infinite approximate Kraus representation.

Theorem 4.4.

Let NN be a diffuse factor equipped with an extremal almost periodic state φ\varphi, and let F≤NF\leq N be a finite dimensional subfactor for which

φ=φ|F⊗φ|Fc\varphi=\varphi|_{F}\otimes\varphi|_{F^{c}}

Suppose T:F→NT\colon F\to N is a normal unital completely positive map satisfying φ∘T=φ|F\varphi\circ T=\varphi|_{F} and σtφ∘T=T∘σtφ|F\sigma_{t}^{\varphi}\circ T=T\circ\sigma_{t}^{\varphi|_{F}}. Then for every δ>0\delta>0 there exists a sequence (an)n∈ℕ⊂Nφ(a_{n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subset N^{\varphi} such that

∑n=1∞an∗​an=∑n=1∞an​an∗=1\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_{n}^{*}a_{n}=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_{n}a_{n}^{*}=1

and

‖T⁡(x)−∑n=1∞an∗​x​an‖≤δ​‖x‖\left\|T(x)-\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_{n}^{*}xa_{n}\right\|\leq\delta\|x\|

for all x∈Fx\in F.

T⁡(x)=∑i=1nbi∗​x​bi,T(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}b_{i}^{*}xb_{i},

for all x∈Fx\in F. In particular, this gives

∑i=1nbi∗​bi=T⁡(1)=1.\sum_{i=1}^{n}b_{i}^{*}b_{i}=T(1)=1.

Let ℰF:N→F\mathcal{E}_{F}\colon N\to F to be σφ\sigma^{\varphi}-preserving conditional expectation. Using φ∘T=φ|F\varphi\circ T=\varphi|_{F} and bi∈Nφb_{i}\in N^{\varphi}, we have for x∈Fx\in F

⟨ℰF​(∑i=1dbi​bi∗),x⟩φ=⟨∑i=1dbi​bi∗,x⟩φ=⟨1,∑i=1dbi∗​x​bi⟩φ=⟨1,T⁡(x)⟩φ=⟨1,x⟩φ.\left\langle\mathcal{E}_{F}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{d}b_{i}b_{i}^{*}\right),x\right\rangle_{\varphi}=\left\langle\sum_{i=1}^{d}b_{i}b_{i}^{*},x\right\rangle_{\varphi}=\left\langle 1,\sum_{i=1}^{d}b_{i}^{*}xb_{i}\right\rangle_{\varphi}=\left\langle 1,T(x)\right\rangle_{\varphi}=\left\langle 1,x\right\rangle_{\varphi}.

Hence ℰF​(∑i=1dbi​bi∗)=1\mathcal{E}_{F}(\sum_{i=1}^{d}b_{i}b_{i}^{*})=1.

Now, apply Lemma 4.3 to ∑i=1dbi​bi∗\sum_{i=1}^{d}b_{i}b_{i}^{*} to find α=∑j=1dtj​Ad​(uj)∈conv⁡{Ad​(u):u∈𝒰⁡(Fc∩Nφ)}\alpha=\sum_{j=1}^{d}t_{j}\text{Ad}\left(u_{j}\right)\in\conv\{\text{Ad}\left(u\right)\colon u\in\mathcal{U}(F^{c}\cap N^{\varphi})\} satisfying

‖α⁡(∑i=1nbi​bi∗)−1‖<δ2.\left\|\alpha\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}b_{i}b_{i}^{*}\right)-1\right\|<\frac{\delta}{2}.

6. Proof of Theorem C

Using either [Izu93, Theorem 4.7] when JJ is finite or [Tho19, Example 1] when JJ is infinte, it follows that πφ​(𝒪J)′′\pi_{\varphi}(\mathcal{O}_{J})^{\prime\prime} is a separable injective type III\mathrm{III} factor. Thus by Theorem A it suffices to show φ\varphi is extremal almost periodic with Sd​(φ)=Λ\text{Sd}(\varphi)=\Lambda. The generators of 𝒪J\mathcal{O}_{J} being eigenoperators with respect to φ\varphi implies the almost periodicity of φ\varphi, and moreover that Sd​(φ)⊂Λ\text{Sd}(\varphi)\subset\Lambda. Since Sd​(φ)\text{Sd}(\varphi) contains generators of the group Λ\Lambda, we will obtain Sd​(φ)=Λ\text{Sd}(\varphi)=\Lambda once we know the former is a group. Therefore the proof will be complete once we have argued that φ\varphi is extremal, and this is essentially already contained in the proof of [Tho19, Theorem 5].

Indeed, [Tho19, Theorem 5] asserts that the Connes spectrum (see [Tak03, Section XI.2]) of the modular automorphism group of σφ\sigma^{\varphi} is given by

Γ⁡(σφ)=Λ¯.\Gamma(\sigma^{\varphi})=\overline{\Lambda}.

In fact, for each projection qq in the center of (πφ​(𝒪J)′′)φ(\pi_{\varphi}(\mathcal{O}_{J})^{\prime\prime})^{\varphi} and each j∈Jj\in J, in the proof of [Tho19, Theorem 5] Thomsen exhibits a partial isometry w∈(πφ​(𝒪J)′′)(φ,μ⁡(j))w\in(\pi_{\varphi}(\mathcal{O}_{J})^{\prime\prime})^{(\varphi,\mu(j))} with q​w​q≠0qwq\neq 0. It follows that

μ⁡(J)⊂Sd​(φ|q​πφ​(𝒪J)′′​q)\mu(J)\subset\text{Sd}(\varphi|_{q\pi_{\varphi}(\mathcal{O}_{J})^{\prime\prime}q})

for all such qq. Equip Λ\Lambda with the discrete topology, let GG be its compact dual, and G​↷𝛼​πφ​(𝒪J)′′G\overset{\alpha}{\curvearrowright}\pi_{\varphi}(\mathcal{O}_{J})^{\prime\prime} be the point modular extension of the modular automorphism group of φ\varphi. Then the above, in conjunction with [Con74, Equation (1)], shows that

μ​(J)⊂Sp​(α(q)),\mu(J)\subset\text{Sp}(\alpha^{(q)}),

where α(q)\alpha^{(q)} is the restriction of α\alpha to q​M​qqMq and Sp​(α(q))\text{Sp}(\alpha^{(q)}) is its Arveson spectrum (see [Tak03, Section XI.1]). Using [Con73, Proposition 2.2.2] we see that

μ⁡(J)⊂⋂qSp​(α(q))=Γ⁡(α).\mu(J)\subset\bigcap_{q}\text{Sp}(\alpha^{(q)})=\Gamma(\alpha).

But since the Connes spectrum of α\alpha is a subgroup of Λ\Lambda it follows that Γ⁡(α)=Λ\Gamma(\alpha)=\Lambda. This in turn implies (πφ​(𝒪J)′′)α=(πφ​(𝒪J)′′)φ(\pi_{\varphi}(\mathcal{O}_{J})^{\prime\prime})^{\alpha}=(\pi_{\varphi}(\mathcal{O}_{J})^{\prime\prime})^{\varphi} is a factor by [Con73, Theorem 2.4.1]. That is, φ\varphi is extremal. □\hfill\square
